claim: src/units/ui/processor.py::close_open_positions (the /closeall operator command) always forwards sl_order_id=None, tp_order_id=None to close_open_position(), so a manual close-all on a Bybit partial-TP/SL account never cancels the position's resting qty-scoped legs.
evidence: Read src/units/ui/processor.py in full. The SELECT at ~line 1633 is `SELECT id, symbol, direction, position_size, strategy_name, account_id FROM trades WHERE ...` -- it never fetches sl_order_id/tp_order_id. At ~line 1722: `sl_order_id=row.get("sl_order_id") if hasattr(row, "get") else None, tp_order_id=row.get("tp_order_id") if hasattr(row, "get") else None`. `row` is a sqlite3.Row (conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row, set a few lines above the SELECT). `python3 -c "import sqlite3; print(hasattr(sqlite3.Row, 'get'))"` -> `False` -- sqlite3.Row has no .get() method, so hasattr is always False and the ternary always takes the else branch, independent of and in addition to the SELECT not fetching those columns. The subagent that found this also wrote a standalone repro (seeded a trades row with sl_order_id='SL-123', tp_order_id='TP-456', ran the literal SELECT+access code) confirming both values resolve to None every time.
expected: close_open_position() receives the row's real sl_order_id/tp_order_id so Bybit's qty-scoped partial-TP/SL legs get best-effort-cancelled after a manual close (per the docstring on execute.close_open_position, src/units/accounts/execute.py:3118-3124).
actual: Always receives sl_order_id=None, tp_order_id=None, reproducing the exact leg-accumulation defect named in the code's own adjacent comment: BL-20260721-BYBIT2-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP / BL-20260825-CLOSE-SIDE-LEG-CANCEL-IS-WIRED-AT-1-OF-10-CALL-SITES (that incident: bybit_1/ETHUSDT, 9.33 stop vs 5.59 position, 167%, 12 stray legs).
population: Every call to /closeall (close_open_positions()) against any Bybit account with a still-open trade whose journal row carries sl_order_id/tp_order_id -- i.e. any account run in Bybit's partial-TP/SL bracket mode. Not exercised for full-close paths that don't go through this function.
detector: tests/test_s031_pr4_closeall_helper.py::test_dispatches_to_execute_close_open_position exists and is green (16/16 passed, `python3 -m pytest tests/test_s031_pr4_closeall_helper.py -q`), but it only asserts the kwarg was passed (`captured.get('sl_order_id', unset) is not unset`), not that it carries the row's real value -- and its `_insert_trade` fixture never seeds sl_order_id/tp_order_id, so it cannot catch this. Needed: seed non-null values in the fixture and assert the forwarded kwargs equal them.
proposed_fix: Add sl_order_id, tp_order_id to the SELECT; replace the always-false hasattr ternary with a direct row['sl_order_id'] read (sqlite3.Row supports __getitem__ by column name); strengthen the existing regression test per the detector note.

evidence: Read src/exchange/bybit_connector.py in full: line 98, `positions = self.exchange.fetch_positions(params={"category": "spot"})`. The method's own docstring is self-contradictory: 'linear perpetuals require params={"category": "spot"}' -- spot and linear are mutually exclusive Bybit v5 categories. Corroborated elsewhere in the same repo: src/units/accounts/clients.py:1516-1533 explicitly special-cases `category == "spot"` to skip the venue call entirely, commented 'return an empty list so callers do not surface a phantom no positions warning derived from a mis-categorised v5 /position/list query.' The account's real category is resolved by _bybit_category() (src/units/accounts/execute.py:88-107), which returns 'linear' for market_type: linear accounts (bybit_2, the live book per CLAUDE.md) -- BybitConnector.get_positions() never reads market_type at all. Consumer traced: src/runtime/risk_counters.py:41-51 inject_runtime_counters() calls exchange_client.get_positions() to populate CURRENT_OPEN_POSITIONS, which gates MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS in src/runtime/orders.py:150-159 safe_place_order().
expected: get_positions() resolves category from the account's actual market_type (as the rest of the account layer does) so CURRENT_OPEN_POSITIONS reflects real exposure.
actual: Always queries category="spot"; for any linear-perp Bybit account this returns [] unconditionally -- CURRENT_OPEN_POSITIONS silently reads 0 regardless of real open positions. The failure is invisible twice over: BybitConnector itself swallows the exception path (logs at WARNING, never raises), so the separate operator alert built for this class of failure (tests/test_silent_except_sweep.py::test_positions_fetch_failure_reports_warn) never fires either, because that alert only fires when the caller sees an actual exception, which this code never lets escape.
population: grep -rn MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS config/ *.env* *.service across the repo -> no hits, so the guard this feeds is currently a no-op regardless of this bug (rated high, not critical, for that reason). No test in tests/ asserts the category param BybitConnector.get_positions() actually sends -- grepped tests/ for BybitConnector + get_positions/category together, zero hits. Contrast: tests/test_set_leverage_preflight.py:99 DOES assert category=="linear" for a sibling leverage-preflight call, so the repo already has the pattern and simply never applied it here.
detector: None exists today. Needed: a unit test on BybitConnector.get_positions() mocking self.exchange.fetch_positions and asserting category matches the account's actual market_type (or at minimum is "linear", not "spot"), following the pattern already used in test_set_leverage_preflight.py.
proposed_fix: Thread the account's market_type (or resolved category, matching _bybit_category()) into BybitConnector.get_positions() and use it instead of the hardcoded "spot" literal; add the missing test.

claim: src/units/ui/data_loaders.py resolves TRADE_JOURNAL_DB by preferring whichever of [canonical path, repo-root legacy path] exists on disk first, so if the canonical $DATA_DIR/trade_journal.db is briefly or permanently absent while a stray REPO_ROOT/trade_journal.db exists, the module silently reads the stray file instead -- contradicting its own header comment that claims the legacy candidate was already dropped, and invisible to the canonical-db-resolver CI guard.
evidence: Read src/units/ui/data_loaders.py:1-90 in full. Lines 44-46 comment: 'The legacy src/bot/trade_journal.db candidate was dropped -- it was a stray duplicate journal we are eliminating.' Lines 47-52 (the actual code): `_TJ_CANDIDATES = [_trade_journal_db_path(), os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "trade_journal.db")]; TRADE_JOURNAL_DB = next((p for p in _TJ_CANDIDATES if p and os.path.exists(p)), _trade_journal_db_path())` -- a second, repo-root candidate is still present and is preferred over the canonical path whenever the canonical file doesn't exist yet but the repo-root one does. The subagent that found this reproduced it directly: set DATA_DIR to an empty temp dir (canonical path absent), pre-created a stray trade_journal.db at repo root, reloaded the module fresh -> data_loaders.TRADE_JOURNAL_DB resolved to the stray repo-root path, not the (absent) canonical one. `python3 scripts/check_canonical_db_resolver.py --list` reports clean (exit 0) over this exact file -- the guard's regexes match `"trade_journal.db"` string literals and env-var reads directly, but this is `os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "trade_journal.db")`, a shape the guard's own test suite explicitly allowlists as safe (test_allows_repo_anchored_join) without accounting for the existence-based next() selection wrapping it. Reachability: this module is imported directly by the live web API (src/web/api/routers/diag.py, multiple call sites ~2286-3652) and by the deployed Telegram bot service; TRADE_JOURNAL_DB is a module-level constant computed once at import time and used by 7+ read functions.
expected: TRADE_JOURNAL_DB should always resolve to the canonical $DATA_DIR-anchored path (or fail loudly / obviously if that path is genuinely absent), never silently substitute an unrelated repo-root file.
actual: Silently prefers whichever candidate happens to exist on disk, so a stray or resurrected repo-root trade_journal.db can shadow the canonical store without any error, warning, or CI signal.
population: In this sandbox's checkout, no trade_journal.db exists at either the canonical or repo-root path currently (DATA_DIR unset, so both candidates happen to coincide at REPO_ROOT here) -- so the divergence is not observable in this container as-is; it was reproduced by the subagent using an explicit temp-DATA_DIR + planted stray-file scenario, matching the real deployment shape where DATA_DIR=/data/bot-data on the live VM differs from REPO_ROOT. tests/test_canonical_db_resolver.py (23/23 passing) does not cover this file or this selection pattern at all.
detector: None. Either drop the repo-root fallback candidate entirely (matching what the file's own comment already claims is true), or add a canonical-db-resolver guard rule that flags an existence-based preference/fallback wrapping an otherwise-allowlisted repo-anchored join. Either way, add a regression test reproducing the empty-canonical + stray-repo-root-file scenario.
proposed_fix: Remove os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "trade_journal.db") from _TJ_CANDIDATES so the constant always resolves to the canonical resolver's answer, matching the module's own stated intent.

claim: src/core/instrument_profile.py::InstrumentProfile.round_qty() truncates via float division and int() rather than rounding, so it silently under-sizes by one whole qty_step on common inputs that land fractionally under an integer boundary due to IEEE-754 imprecision -- currently dead code with zero callers.
evidence: src/core/instrument_profile.py:123-128: `steps = int(qty / self.qty_step); return round(steps * self.qty_step, 8)`. Verified live: InstrumentProfile(..., qty_step=0.01).round_qty(0.29) -> 0.28 (not 0.29); round_qty(19.99) -> 19.98 (not 19.99). Root cause: 0.29/0.01 == 28.999999999999996 in IEEE-754 float, and int() truncates toward zero instead of rounding, so a value that should land exactly on a step boundary loses a whole step whenever the division comes in fractionally under the integer. grep for `.round_qty(` across src/ and scripts/ -> zero callers outside the method's own definition; zero hits in tests/ either.

actual: Returns 0.28 -- a silent under-fill by exactly one qty_step whenever the float division lands fractionally under the true integer step count.
population: Zero production callers found (grepped src/ and scripts/ exhaustively) -- this is dead code today, not an active sizing error. It is the only qty-rounding helper on the typed InstrumentProfile, so a future PR reaching for step-rounding logic would plausibly wire this in as-is.
detector: None. Needed: a regression test with inputs like 0.29/0.01 and 19.99/0.01 asserting the exact expected step-aligned value, once fixed.
proposed_fix: steps = round(qty / self.qty_step) (or math.floor(qty / self.qty_step + 1e-9) if floor-toward-safe is the intended semantics) instead of int() truncation.
disposition: filed as low-priority dead-code fix, not filed to the pipeline store (currently unreachable, no due_when condition beyond 'someone wires this in' which the pipeline schema has no good way to express as an observation) -- noted here so a future lane wiring InstrumentProfile.round_qty() in sees this first
